chain.label: SAT failed to clean engine compressors after recurring oil leaks in the weeks before the accident
chain.trigger: there was no record that SAT cleaned the compressors of the engines on N517SJ following any of the incidents

chain.label: Tar-like oil residue accumulated in the No. 1 and No. 2 engine compressors and air bleed valves
chain.trigger: internal surfaces and components of the numbers 1 and 2 engine compressors were coated with a tar-like residue... impeded the proper actuation of some of the 5th stage valves

caused_by.evidence: the failure of SAT maintenance to clean the engine compressors following oil leaks... allowed the accumulation of oil residues in the engines

chain.label: First officer candidate with no prior L-382/C-130 experience was flying the approach under instruction
chain.trigger: the airplane was being flown by a first officer candidate who had no previous L-382/C-130 flight experience

chain.label: First officer established an incorrect, high pitch attitude near touchdown
chain.trigger: the captain had been concerned before touchdown that the pitch attitude established by the first officer was incorrect for landing

caused_by.evidence: first officer candidate who had no previous L-382/C-130 flight experience

chain.label: Nos. 1 and 2 engines failed to respond to throttle advance, decelerating about 40 percent during the go-around
chain.trigger: the numbers 1 and 2 engines both failed to respond normally, and in fact decelerated about 40 percent following throttle advancement at the commencement of the go-around

caused_by.evidence: the lack of power section response from the number 1 and 2 engines was directly attributable to the accumulated oil residues in the dirty compressors and air bleed valves
the captain assumed control of the airplane and began a go-around

chain.label: Captain did not promptly recognize that power had been lost from two engines
chain.trigger: it is apparent that the captain either did not recognize promptly that power had been lost from two engines or that the loss of power would potentially render the airplane uncontrollable

caused_by.evidence: the captain had substantial warning that the airplane was experiencing a loss of power from at least one engine, but that information did not become apparent until the go-around had been commenced

chain.label: Crew raised the flap handle to the retracted position, contrary to engine-inoperative emergency procedure
chain.trigger: a crewmember called, 'Flaps up' ... The decision to raise the flaps during the go-around was not only incorrect but it contributed to the cause of the accident

caused_by.evidence: a decision which was contrary to engine inoperative emergency procedures

chain.label: Flap retraction reduced rudder boost hydraulic pressure from 3,000 to 1,300 psi
chain.trigger: the movement of the flap handle to the retracted position would have reduced rudder boost actuator pressure from 3,000 to 1,300 psi

caused_by.evidence: the movement of the flap handle to the retracted position would have reduced rudder boost actuator pressure

chain.label: Vmca exceeded available airspeed; airplane entered an uncontrollable left yaw and steepening bank
chain.trigger: Vmca was significantly higher than the actual air speed and the airplane began an uncontrollable yaw to the left

caused_by.evidence: the yawing moment caused by the most adverse thrust asymmetry, occurring when the two operating engines are at high power, is significantly higher than the yawing moment with only one engine inoperative
a sudden decrease in rudder deflection (despite the efforts of the crew)... Vmca was significantly higher than the actual air speed

chain.label: Captain continued the go-around instead of relanding once heading and roll control could not be maintained
chain.trigger: the captain continued the go-around until control was lost rather than attempting to reland at the first indication that heading and roll control could not be maintained

caused_by.evidence: the Safety Board also believes that the captain's decision contributed to the consequences of the accident

chain.label: Airplane struck the airfield perimeter fence and terrain in a steep, left wing-low, nose-low attitude
chain.trigger: the airplane collided with the airfield perimeter fence in a nose-low and steep left wing low attitude

caused_by.evidence: the captain continued the go-around until control was lost
a left bank at low altitude which steepened until the airplane collided with the airfield perimeter fence

chain.label: All five crewmembers were fatally injured
chain.trigger: All five crewmen were fatally injured

caused_by.evidence: the causes of death were attributed to multiple traumatic injuries
